static._archetype_note: JUDGMENT CALL: 'services-project' is the closer fit of the three named archetypes -- revenue is billed per project/turnaround with 'project timing, field utilization, mobilization, and customer acceptance' driving monthly volatility (IC Memo), working capital is genuinely collections-led (customer-level AR aging with named 'Collection plan' accounts tracked separately every month), and the company is monitored via 'collections, project-margin, liquidity, and required-principal review' -- all project-services framing, not consumer-inventory (no inventory pledged or tracked) or a fleet-utilization asset-heavy-industrial read. COUNTERPOINT flagged for the analyst: the FY2024 Annual Balance Sheet shows 'Fixed and other assets' of $121,347,780.77 -- fully 77% of total assets ($157,589,224.69) -- which is unusually large for a pure people/project services business and could reflect either genuine owned inspection/testing equipment and facilities, or goodwill/intangibles from the sponsor's acquisition of the business (purchase-price allocation), or both; the annual statement does not break the line down further and the monthly package never reports fixed assets at all. If this balance is substantially operating equipment rather than goodwill, 'asset-heavy-industrial' could be the better-fitting archetype -- flagged for analyst confirmation.

our_view.thesis_status: This credit has moved from comfortably compliant to two consecutive quarters of covenant breach, compounded by two separate, confirmed-independent reporting-integrity failures in the same window -- pillars 3 and 4 are graded 'broken' above, not merely 'pressured'. TTM FCCR has declined for five straight quarters: 1.6245x (2025-Q1) -> 1.6099x (Q2) -> 1.6436x (Q3) -> 1.2365x (Q4, the first quarter to fully reflect Amendment 1's 2.00%/month amortization step-up) -> 1.0338x (2026-Q1, BREACH -- WAIVED) -> 0.9192x (2026-Q2, BREACH -- WAIVED). The underlying driver so far looks MECHANICAL rather than purely operational: TTM Covenant EBITDA has actually been broadly stable-to-growing across the same window (~$25.2M at 2024-09 to ~$30.1M at 2026-06, EBITDA margin holding in the ~17-20% range every month checked) -- the deterioration is concentrated in the Fixed Charges denominator (required principal 10x'd by Amendment 1), not a collapse in operating performance. That is a real distinction (this is not (yet) a business in decline) but it does not change the credit fact: the covenant has been breached for two straight quarters, the only relief obtained (the Temporary Limited Waiver) explicitly does NOT deem either test compliant and has now EXPIRED (2026-06-30), and there is no evidence of any new waiver or amendment executed ahead of the September 30, 2026 Test Date -- 15 days from this review. On top of the covenant trajectory, the borrower's own compliance process failed twice in a row: BOTH the March 31 and June 30, 2026 quarterly certificates were originally submitted using a single-month FCCR calculation instead of the agreement-required trailing-twelve-month measurement (caught only by lender query each time), and a SEPARATE March 2026 revenue/cost reclassification error (a $617,841.06 understatement, EBITDA-neutral) was found and corrected in July 2026. Two independent, confirmed-separate correction episodes landing in the same two quarters is a legitimate governance/controls flag in its own right, independent of the FCCR magnitude -- per the standing guidance, this alone would argue against defaulting to watchlist 'off' even if the covenant were compliant.
our_view.what_would_change_our_mind: Watchlist could move toward 'off'/trajectory toward 'stable' if: (a) new waiver or amendment authority is executed covering the September 30, 2026 Test Date before it arrives, removing the immediate uncovered-breach exposure; (b) TTM Covenant EBITDA growth outpaces the now-stepped-up amortization enough to visibly arrest the five-quarter FCCR decline (even a flattening at 2026-Q3, rather than continued deterioration, would be meaningful); and (c) at least one clean quarterly certificate cycle is delivered with no lender query and no correction notice, evidencing the compliance-preparation process has actually been fixed rather than merely caught twice. Conversely, an unwaived breach at the September 30, 2026 Test Date, a third correction/restatement episode, or a genuine EBITDA decline (as opposed to the amortization-driven denominator effect seen so far) would harden 'deteriorating' further and could warrant escalation beyond routine watchlist monitoring.
